transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
British Police Sunday arrested five men near an Air Force base being used on a limited
basis by the U.S. in its war on Iran.
The five are being held on suspicion of preparing an act of terrorism.
Chief Constable Maggie Blythe says that while dozens of homes near the base remain evacuated,
the situation there is now returning to normal.
Again, I can't go into details, but I can give reassurance that we believe the matter
to be contained and as a set of agencies working together across Gloucestershire we're gathering
and responding to local intelligence all the time.
Explosives teams are now examining three vehicles located near the base.
Diesel prices have slipped a little, but the war in Iran continues to strain the nation's
fuel supplies.
As NPR's Windsor Johnston reports, the concern now is how long higher costs could be working
their way into household bills.
Farmers in many parts of the country are still paying much more to run combines, tractors
and trucks during the fall harvest.
Higher fuel costs can move through the food supply chain, and the pressure may last.
Diesel and home heating oil draw on the same tight fuel supply as winter approaches.
Some shipping costs are set by contractors, so shoppers may not see the full effect right
away.
U.S. fuel inventories are low, leaving little cushion if supplies are disrupted again.
That's why a modest drop in diesel prices offers only limited relief.
The Trump administration has discussed expanding U.S. refining capacity, but has not announced
an immediate measure to lower prices.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
The White House has told Congress it plans to cancel $810 million in health care and
educational-related programs.
As NPR's Mara Liasson reports, at least one prominent Republican isn't happy with that
announcement.
In a statement on X, Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins said the move,
known as a pocket rescission, is unlawful.
Collins, an incumbent Republican from Maine running for re-election, also said that the
rescissions were intended to "undermine Congress's constitutional power of the purse."
Regardless of how this separation of powers dispute is resolved, there are other cuts
to social safety net programs that were in the one big beautiful bill that are just now
kicking in, and they're hurting people who depend on Medicaid and food assistance.
That's another reason, along with higher prices at the pump or 7% mortgages, that voters say
they are angry and economically stressed—a bad sign for the incumbent party just weeks
away from the election.
Mara Liasson, NPR News.
That powerful nor'easter off the East Coast is continuing to cause flooding in low-lying
areas of New York and New Jersey at this hour.
War has also been knocked out to thousands of homes in New England, and at least one
death has been linked to the storm.
There's better news out west, though, where Hurricane NOLO is moving away from the Hawaiian
Islands after leaving relatively little damage.
You're listening to NPR News.
There will be music again in Cleveland.
Musicians at the Cleveland Orchestra went on strike Friday, demanding better compensation
and a voice in auditions.
The Musicians' Union announced a New Deal Sunday afternoon, one they say includes better
pay, a role in auditions, and improved safety measures.
The orchestra is now expected to go ahead with a planned European tour.
An updated version of the Golden Age musical "Damn Yankees" is coming to Broadway in
the spring.
The production, which stars Neil Patrick Harris and Julian Huff, was announced Sunday afternoon
at Yankee Stadium.
Jeff London has more.
The Yankees game was rained out, but in the press room, where manager Aaron Boone normally
meets reporters, a bunch of Broadway folk gathered for a different kind of press conference.
Neil Patrick Harris will be playing Applegate, the Faustian character who transforms a middle-aged
Baltimore fan into a young baseball star so his team can beat the Yankees.
Some of the outdated aspects of the show have been rewritten, and Major League Baseball
and MLB studios are co-producers.
Damn Yankees begins performances in March, and its opening day is in April.
For NPR News, I'm Jeff London in New York.
Police in Columbia say they have captured the wife and daughter of Ecuadoran gang leader
Jose Adolfo Macias Villamar.
He was extradited to the U.S. last year on drug trafficking charges.
Police say the two women are wanted in Ecuador to face money laundering charges.
They were arrested in an operation that was backed by the FBI.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: British police arrest five men near U.S. Air Force base on terrorism suspicion
War in Iran strains fuel supplies; diesel prices slip but concerns remain about costs
White House plans to cancel 810 million dollars in health care and education programs
Nor'easter causes flooding in New York and New Jersey; one death reported from storm
Hurricane Nolo moves away from Hawaiian Islands after causing relatively little damage
Cleveland Orchestra musicians end strike with deal including better pay and audition voice
Updated 'Damn Yankees' musical starring Neil Patrick Harris coming to Broadway in spring
Colombian police capture wife and daughter of Ecuadoran gang leader Jose Adolfo Macias Villamar
